intended_object: The inverse of the Conway normal-form isomorphism for omnific integers. It sends a universe-bounded Hahn series with real coefficients and nonnegative Conway exponents (written as nonpositive exponents in the order dual), whose constant coefficient is an integer, to the omnific integer Σ r_i ω^{a_i} it represents. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body moves the coefficients onto surreal exponents. It turns the cardinality bound on the support into `Small.{u}` and transfers well-foundedness through `toDual`. It then evaluates with `SurrealHahnSeries.toSurreal`, which is the normal-form sum. Membership in the omnific integers comes from the normal-form characterization: every exponent is ≥ 0 and the constant coefficient is an integer. The file proves that the full normal form of the result equals the input series, and the normal-form map is injective, so the value is uniquely determined. It also proves both round-trip identities with `toSmallSupportIntegerPart`. So this really is the inverse of the normal-form isomorphism Oz_u ≃ ℤ + ℝ((No^{≤0}))_κ. The surreal, real-coefficient and universe-cardinal setting is part of what the object is, so the definition is not too narrow, and Mathlib has no counterpart because it does not define surreal normal forms or omnific integers.
